=== rolldown babel plugin readme ===
# @rolldown/plugin-babel [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@rolldown/plugin-babel.svg)](https://npmx.dev/package/@rolldown/plugin-babel)

Rolldown plugin for transforming code with [Babel](https://babeljs.io/).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @rolldown/plugin-babel @babel/core
```

If you are using TypeScript, you will also need to install `@types/babel__core`:

```bash
pnpm add -D @types/babel__core
```

## Usage

```js
import babel from '@rolldown/plugin-babel'

export default {
  plugins: [
    babel({
      plugins: ['@babel/plugin-proposal-throw-expressions'],
    }),
  ],
}
```

The plugin automatically configures Babel's parser for `.jsx`, `.ts`, and `.tsx` files.

> **Note:** This plugin does not load Babel configuration files (e.g., `babel.config.js`, `.babelrc`). All Babel options must be passed directly through the plugin options.

## Options

### `include`

- **Type:** `string | RegExp | (string | RegExp)[]`
- **Default:** `/\.(?:[jt]sx?|[cm][jt]s)(?:$|\?)/`

Only files matching the pattern will be processed.

Note that this option receives [the syntax supported by babel](https://babeljs.io/docs/options#matchpattern) instead of picomatch.

### `exclude`

- **Type:** `string | RegExp | (string | RegExp)[]`
- **Default:** `/[\/\\]node_modules[\/\\]|\0rolldown\/runtime\.js/`

Files matching the pattern will be skipped. The default also excludes Rolldown's runtime helper module (`\0rolldown/runtime.js`) so that Babel does not transform Rolldown's internal runtime code. If you override `exclude`, you are responsible for re-adding any of these entries you still want to skip.

Note that this option receives [the syntax supported by babel](https://babeljs.io/docs/options#matchpattern) instead of picomatch.

### `sourceMap`

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`

Set to `false` to skip source map generation for better performance.

### `presets`

- **Type:** `(babel.PresetItem | RolldownBabelPreset)[]`

List of Babel presets to apply. Supports both standard Babel presets and Rolldown-enhanced presets with per-file filtering (see [Rolldown Babel Presets](#rolldown-babel-presets)).

### `plugins`

- **Type:** `babel.PluginItem[]`

List of Babel plugins to apply.

### `overrides`

- **Type:** `InnerTransformOptions[]`

Array of additional configurations that are merged into the current configuration. Use with Babel's `test`/`include`/`exclude` options to conditionally apply overrides.

content.text:
Two answers, depending on which "React Compiler" you mean:

**No — not VoidZero's native one.** That's `oxc-transform-react` (the Rust port, latest `0.148.0`), used via `react({ compiler: true })`. It's not installed here. Your `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.1` *does* expose `compiler?: boolean | ReactCompilerPluginOptions`, so the door is open — but its README still flags native support as experimental.

**Yes — you're on the latest Babel React Compiler.** `babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0` is the current `latest` tag (there's an `experimental` channel too, if you're feeling like the rest of this dep tree). Supporting packages are all at latest as well: `@rolldown/plugin-babel@0.2.3`, `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.1`.

And it's genuinely running, not just wired — `vite.config.ts:31-34` matches the documented `react(), babel({ presets: [reactCompilerPreset()] })` pattern exactly, and the built output has `react/compiler-runtime` imports across the client chunks (`.output/public/assets/*.js`, `dist/client/assets/*.js`).

One note: `0.148.0` isn't "newer than 1.0.0" — different implementation, different versioning scheme (oxc monorepo). Switching would be a lateral move to a faster-but-experimental transformer, not an upgrade.

Want me to try it? The delta is small: add `oxc-transform-react`, change `viteReact()` → `viteReact({ compiler: true })`, and drop the `babel({...})` block plus `@rolldown/plugin-babel`, `babel-plugin-react-compiler`, and `@types/babel__core`. Worth being cautious given your prerendered SSR build.

Minor unrelated thing: `@babel/core@8.0.1` is a required peer for the Babel path but isn't in your `devDependencies` — it resolves transitively today, which is fine until it isn't.

Done — you're on VoidZero's Rust React Compiler now.

**Changes** (uncommitted, `package.json` still carries your earlier dep bumps):
- `vite.config.ts`: dropped the `babel({...})` block and both its imports, `viteReact()` → `viteReact({ compiler: true })`
- Added `oxc-transform-react`, removed `@rolldown/plugin-babel`, `babel-plugin-react-compiler`, `@types/babel__core`
- `package-lock.json` shed ~580 lines net (the whole Babel tree went with it)

**Verified working:**
- `vp check` clean, `vp test run` 16/16 passing
- Clean `vp build` succeeded, prerendered all 9 pages
- Compiler active in the build: `react/compiler-runtime` split into its own chunk and referenced by 9 client chunks. Two chunks (`FloatingOrbs-BhzlTVTg.js`, `services-DcxptV_V.js`) came out **byte-identical** to the pre-switch Babel build — same content hash — which is about as direct as equivalence evidence gets
- Direct probe of `oxc-transform-react` on your sources confirms real memoization: `FloatingOrbs.tsx` → 3 memo caches, `routes/index.tsx` → 3, `Layout/Header.tsx` → 1
- Dev server boots in ~2s, serves 200, transformed modules contain both `compiler-runtime` **and** `$RefreshReg$`/`$RefreshSig$` — Fast Refresh is intact (the compiler plugin takes over JSX + refresh injection rather than losing it)

**Two things worth knowing:**

`oxc-transform-react` installed at **0.145.0**, not the 0.148.0 I quoted earlier. `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.1` pins the peer to `^0.145.0`, which on a `0.x` version means `>=0.145.0 <0.146.0` — so 0.145.0 *is* the latest compatible release, and npm did the right thing. You'll get newer oxc versions as plugin-react bumps its peer range.

`CommandAgent.tsx` bails out of compilation with `(BuildHIR::lowerStatement) Handle TryStatement with a finalizer ('finally') clause`. That's a recoverable bail — the file just ships uncompiled, same as Babel would have done. If you want to see these, `viteReact({ compiler: { logDiagnostics: true } })` surfaces them during builds.

The experimental caveat still stands, so I'd give the deployed site a click-through before you ship it. Want me to commit this?

# syntax = docker/dockerfile:1

# Node is used only to build; the runtime image is Bun (see BUN_VERSION below)
ARG NODE_VERSION=24
# Pinned to a patch: Bun.markdown/Bun APIs used at runtime are version-sensitive.
ARG BUN_VERSION=1.4.0

# Throw-away build stage to reduce size of final image
FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-slim AS build

WORKDIR /app

# Install Vite+ CLI (curl needed for installer)
RUN apt-get update -qq && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
# The installer moved its bin dir (~/.vite-plus/bin -> ~/.local/share/vite-plus/bin);
# keep both so the build works across installer versions and cached layers.
ENV PATH="/root/.local/share/vite-plus/bin:/root/.vite-plus/bin:$PATH"

# Install dependencies
COPY --link package-lock.json package.json ./
RUN sed -i 's/"prepare": "vp config"/"prepare": "true"/' package.json && \
    npm ci

# Copy application code
COPY --link . .

# Build application (emits .output/ via Nitro)
RUN vp build

# Drop dev dependencies for the final image
RUN npm prune --omit=dev


# Final stage for app image
FROM oven/bun:${BUN_VERSION}-slim

LABEL fly_launch_runtime="TanStack Start"

# App lives here
WORKDIR /app

# Set production environment
ENV NODE_ENV="production"

# Copy built application
COPY --from=build /app /app

# Start the Nitro node-server output under Bun
EXPOSE 3000
CMD [ "bun", "./.output/server/index.mjs" ]

Yes — one real orphan fell out of it.

**Removed `bun.lock`** (1,318 lines, 164K, tracked). It was already dead weight, and this change made it demonstrably wrong — it still listed `@rolldown/plugin-babel`, `babel-plugin-react-compiler`, and `@types/babel__core` as project deps. Nothing reads it:
- `Dockerfile:31` installs with `npm ci` against `package-lock.json`
- CI runs `vp install`, which resolves the package manager from `packageManager: "npm@11.12.1"` — priority 1 in Vite+'s detection order, ahead of any lockfile (`bun.lock` is priority 7)
- No reference to it anywhere in the repo

Bun is only the *runtime* here (final Docker stage), never the installer. Confirmed after deleting: `vp install` ran clean through npm and didn't write a `devEngines.packageManager` field or regenerate the lockfile.

**`@babel/core@8.0.1` is gone from the top level** — it was there solely as `@rolldown/plugin-babel`'s peer, which is why it never needed to be in your `devDependencies`. The `@babel/core@7.29.7` copies that remain are nested under `@tanstack/router-plugin` and `@tanstack/start-plugin-core`; those aren't yours to remove.

**Nothing else to clean.** No `.babelrc` or `babel.config.*` ever existed, and `tsconfig.json` never referenced the babel types.

Re-validated after the cleanup: `vp check` clean, 16/16 tests passing.

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Switch React Compiler from Babel to oxc-transform-react

Replace the Babel-based React Compiler pipeline with VoidZero's native Rust
port, available in @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1 as `react({ compiler: true })`.

- Drop the `babel()` plugin block and `reactCompilerPreset` from vite.config.ts
- Remove @rolldown/plugin-babel, babel-plugin-react-compiler, @types/babel__core
  (this also drops the top-level @babel/core, which only existed as a peer)
- Add oxc-transform-react, pinned by plugin-react's peer range to 0.145.x

Fast Refresh is unaffected: the compiler plugin takes over the JSX transform
and injects the refresh runtime itself, so $RefreshReg$/$RefreshSig$ still
appear in dev-served modules.

Verified the output is equivalent, not just present: two client chunks
(FloatingOrbs, services) came out byte-identical to the Babel build, and
direct transforms confirm real memoization (FloatingOrbs 3 memo caches,
routes/index 3, Header 1). CommandAgent bails out on a try/finally clause,
which Babel did too.

Cleanup enabled by the above:

- Delete bun.lock. It was stale (still listed the three removed Babel deps)
  and unread: the Dockerfile installs via `npm ci` against package-lock.json,
  and `vp install` resolves from the `packageManager: npm@11.12.1` pin, which
  outranks lockfile detection. Bun is only the runtime, never the installer.
- Add /.output to .dockerignore so a local 4.6M build no longer ships in the
  Docker context; the build stage generates it via `vp build` regardless.

Also folds in dependency bumps already pending in the tree: @ai-sdk/groq,
ai, @types/node.

Checks: vp check clean, 16/16 tests passing, docker build exit 0 with all
9 pages prerendered, container serving 200 on / and /blog under Bun.
